Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The warped door is at (1,0,11) at the corridor's end. Max distance 4 ensures the player has navigated to the end of the corridor and is looking at the door.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. Nether wart blocks are at (-1 to 2, 0, 14). Tighter max_distance=3 requires closer approach than the soul_sand milestone, ensuring the player specifically observes these blocks rather than just entering the garden.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. Gray wool blocks are in the western storage room centered at (-8,0,0). Max distance 4 ensures the player has entered the room through the doorway at x=-5 and is observing the wool.

Uses inventory_has because the dried kelp is placed as an item entity on the storage room floor at (-8,1,3) — it is NOT in the player's starting inventory. The player must physically navigate to the storage room and pick it up (auto-pickup on proximity). This verifies collection as the best available proxy for consumption, since no rule type can detect food use directly.

Uses inventory_has for emerald because the armorer villager has a pre-defined diamond→emerald trade via Offers NBT. The player starts with 0 emeralds and the ONLY source of emeralds in this entire scene is the villager trade. Having an emerald in inventory conclusively proves a successful trade occurred.

Uses inventory_has because glazed terracotta drops itself when mined with any pickaxe (player has diamond pickaxe). The player must mine at least one block from the 4-wide × 3-tall terracotta wall at x=8. The item appearing in inventory confirms successful mining.

Uses inventory_has because crafting a diamond helmet places it directly in the player's inventory. The player starts without any diamond helmet, so its presence confirms successful crafting at the crafting table in the Nether garden.

Uses position_near_with_facing with very tight constraints (max_distance=2, facing_tolerance=45°) targeting the anvil at (5,0,14). This is the best available approximation since no rule type can detect custom item names. The extremely close proximity and precise facing required means the player must be in anvil-interaction position, making accidental triggering unlikely.

Uses count_in_box_at_most (kind='mob', max_count=0) because this is a kill/combat task. The Size:1 slime at (10,0,1) splits into 2-4 Size:0 tiny slimes when killed — all must be eliminated. The generous detection box (x=5-12, y=-1 to 5, z=-3 to 5) covers the entire enclosed eastern room ensuring no slime can escape detection while still alive.

Uses position_inside_box because this is a movement/navigation task — the player must physically descend deep into the water pool. The pool spans x=9-11, z=-8 to -3, from y=-2 (surface) to y=-12 (bottom). The box requires the player to reach y=-9 or lower (7+ blocks below water surface), confirming a genuinely deep dive.

scene_description: A Nether-inspired trading outpost with three branching paths from a central torch-lit corridor. NORTH: corridor with wall torches (facing=west, attached to nether_brick pillars at x=2) leads to a warped door (z=11) opening into a fully enclosed Nether garden (z=12-17) with soul sand floor, nether wart blocks, crafting table, and anvil. WEST: storage room (x=-5 to -11, z=-2 to 4) containing gray wool blocks, dried kelp item entity on floor, armorer villager with blast furnace and pre-defined diamond→emerald trade. EAST: mining room (x=5 to 11, z=-2 to 4) with a complete 3-wide × 3-tall terracotta wall at x=8 blocking passage to slime chamber (Size:1 slime), which connects via an opening at z=-2 to a 10-block-deep water pool for diving.
task_text: Navigate this Nether-themed trading outpost. Follow the wall torches along the main corridor to discover three branching areas: (1) NORTH: Open the warped door at the corridor's end to enter the Nether garden with soul sand floor and nether wart blocks. Use the crafting table there to craft a diamond helmet (arrange 5 diamonds in a helmet pattern: 3 across the top row, 1 on each side of the middle row). Then rename your map at the adjacent anvil. (2) WEST: Enter the storage room to find gray wool blocks, pick up and eat the dried kelp from the floor, then sell a diamond to the armorer villager for an emerald. (3) EAST: Mine through the light gray glazed terracotta wall with your diamond pickaxe to reach the slime chamber, defeat the slime with your iron sword, then dive deeply into the water pool beyond.
design_notes: FINAL VERSION incorporating all review fixes: (1) Wall torches use facing=west with nether_brick support pillars at x=2 — torch protrudes west, attaches to block at x+1=2. CORRECT. (2) /xp set @p 30 levels for anvil renaming. (3) Blast furnace at (-10,0,2) adjacent to villager at (-9,0,3) for trade initialization. (4) Villager has pre-defined Offers NBT with diamond→emerald trade (maxUses:999). Format targets MC 1.20.4. (5) Dried kelp spawned as item entity at (-8,1,3) with Age:-32768 (never despawns) and PickupDelay:0 — NOT in player starting inventory. (6) Terracotta wall: 4 wide (z=-1 to z=2) × 3 tall (y=0 to y=2) = 12 blocks at x=8, completely blocking passage from mining area (x=5-7) to slime chamber (x=9-11). (7) Slime is Size:1 (small, 2 HP, splits into 2-4 Size:0 tiny slimes with 1 HP each — total 3-5 kills manageable with iron sword). (8) Nether garden fully enclosed: walls at x=-3, x=6, z=17, and partial wall at z=12 with only the warped door gap at (1,0-1,11). (9) Water pool: 3×6×10 blocks deep (x=9-11, z=-8 to -3, y=-12 to -2) with blackstone containment on all sides and bottom. Entry via air blocks at (9-11, 0/-1, -2) leading down into water. (10) Western storage room doorway: 2-wide air gap at x=-5, z=0-1. (11) Eastern mining room doorway: 2-wide air gap at x=5, z=0-1. (12) Target version: Minecraft 1.20.4 (pre-1.20.5 NBT item format).
